items.title: 🔓 [Fast Company] Expanded pasta recall impacts Walmart’s Bettergoods brand as Listeria contamination fears spread
items.content_html:
Last month, a recall was initiated for select lots of a pasta product sold at Walmart stores nationwide.

The recall stemmed from concerns that the product could be contaminated with Listeria monocytogenes, a bacterium that can cause serious infection and even death.

Now, the Walmart pasta recall has expanded. Here’s what you need to know.

What’s happened?

On October 1, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) published a recall notice about a pasta product.

The product was made by Gias Foods of New York City and sold under Walmart’s Bettergoods brand. However, this is not the first recall notice associated with this product.

Two weeks earlier, on September 15, the original recall of the Gias Foods-produced, Bettergoods-branded pasta was announced.

This original announcement said the recall was limited to only specific lots of the pasta product. However, the new notice posted by the FDA yesterday says that all lots of the Bettergoods pasta product are being recalled.

What is Bettergoods?

Bettergoods is Walmart’s relatively new premium grocery label. As Fast Company reported at the time, Walmart launched the Bettergoods label in 2024 to create a premium private-label brand distinct from its low-cost Great Value brand.

The brand aimed to create a new visual identity for unique products made with higher-quality ingredients—something shoppers with more discretionary dollars would be willing to pay more for.

However, foods sold under the Bettergoods label have been impacted by a few different recalls over the brand’s short lifetime.

Back in October 2024, some of its waffle products were caught up in a larger multi-brand waffle product recall, and just this past August, a Bettergoods Pistachio Nut Butter product was recalled due to Salmonella fears.

What products are being recalled?

For the latest recall, there is only one product involved:

  • Name: Bettergoods Authentic Italian Lemon Alfredo Fettuccine
  • Size: 22 oz
  • UPC: 194346442706

The recall notice states the product is frozen.

The original recall of the product limited units to certain lot numbers. However, the new recall notice says all lot codes of the product are now included in the recall.

Images of the recalled product’s packaging can be found here.

Where was the recalled product sold?

The recalled product was distributed to Walmart stores nationwide.

What is Listeria?

Listeria is a bacterium that can cause a serious infection.

According to the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), about 1,250 people in the United States contract a Listeria infection each year. Of those, about 172 people die from it, giving the infection a high mortality rate.

While a Listeria infection can affect anyone, the infection is particularly dangerous for certain groups of people, including:

  • Pregnant women
  • Newborns
  • Adults aged 65 or older
  • People with weakened immune systems

According to the recall notice, routine sampling by state agriculture services revealed that the recalled pasta may contain the harmful bacteria.

What should I do if I have the recalled product?

You should take the product back to its place of purchase for a refund. You can find out the full details of the recall in the recall notice here.

items.title: [ScienceDaily] Even one strength training session a week could make a difference
items.content_html:
🌾 🔧 🪶 🌲 🏔️ 🔭 ✏️

Strength training may be one of the most powerful tools for staying independent as you age. Age related muscle loss, known as sarcopenia, can make everyday tasks harder while increasing the risk of falls, fractures, and loss of mobility. Research shows that resistance exercises such as squats, weights, resistance bands, and even body weight movements can preserve or rebuild strength, and surprisingly, even one session a week can produce meaningful benefits.

items.title: 🔓 [Fast Company] Grindr is spending $250M to signal that it’s getting serious about LGBTQ+ healthcare
items.content_html:
🌾 🔧 ✏️

Grindr is expanding its footprint in LGBTQ-focused healthcare with its first major acquisition. The dating app is paying $250 million for health startup Freddie, with the aim of fully integrating Freddie’s HIV-prevention telehealth and pharmacy capabilities into a broader Grindr Health offering.

The launch of Grindr Health builds on the company’s telehealth business Woodwork, which launched in 2025 to connect users with medication for weight loss and erectile dysfunction. As of Wednesday, when the acquisition was announced, users can access features from both Freddie and Woodwork through a Grindr Health portal in the app.

Grindr CEO George Arison has long credited the app with helping to make HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) more mainstream. The preventive medication is 99% effective at reducing the sexual transmission of the virus.

As of 2025, the United States reached a record high of more than 644,000 PrEP users, a 10% increase from 2024. But the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention estimates that 2.2 million Americans could benefit from PrEP—meaning the medicine is still reaching less than a third of its potential users in the country, and there’s a lot of room for Grindr’s new business to grow.

“It’s a situation where everybody that can be on this drug should be on this drug, because it’s healthier for them and healthier for people that they meet,” Arison tells Fast Company. “To us, [PrEP access] seems like a natural opportunity and a win-win, to both build a great business as well as do something really important for public health,” he says.

Adding a pharmacy to the gayborhood

Arison says contracting HIV is “the one thing that all gay men are scared of,” suggesting that taking PrEP should be common sense for the app’s users. But mirroring broader U.S. statistics, Grindr reports that only 400,000 of its millions of American users identify as being on PrEP.

“If we achieve the same market share in the U.S. on PrEP that Freddie has in Canada . . . that will mean [an additional] 200,000 people on PrEP, and that will mean about 5,000 people not getting HIV a year,” Arison adds. With the most recent CDC findings showing an estimated 31,800 new HIV infections in the U.S. per year, that means Grindr could play a significant role in driving down HIV infections nationwide.

Adding in more healthcare to complement Woodwork—which initially offered erectile dysfuynction medication and has since expanded to include GLP-1s—is part of Arison’s effort to make users (and investors) see Grindr as a “global gayborhood,” not just a place for hookups. The company has been leveraging AI to build new features that improve the user experience and offer specific insights about people that users might want to connect with.

“Don’t think of Grindr as a dating product. Think of Grindr as a social network that has a very unique pulse on the user base,” he says. “Obviously, we needed to prove to everyone that that’s what we were. This is just a logical next step in that direction.”

Good for health, good for business

As Arison has been expanding his vision for Grindr beyond just connecting people, he’s also been improving the company’s revenue and subscriber base.

In the second quarter of 2026, Grindr reported a revenue of $138 million, a 33% year-over-year increase. Meanwhile, the app’s paying user base continues to grow, with a current 1.4 million users paying for Grindr features including its XTRA and Unlimited subscription tiers, up 16% from last year.

Researchers at Morgan Stanley noted the clear rationale for Grindr’s acquisition of Freddie, pointing to the app’s earlier telehealth success through Woodwork. And even before that launch, Grindr successfully connected more than 2 million users with mpox vaccines in 2022.

The analysts also highlighted Freddie’s strong earning potential for Grindr. The telehealth platform has higher gross margins than its peers, as Freddie generates revenue from referral fees to entities receiving federal discounts through the U.S.’s 340B Drug Pricing Program.

With each active patient estimated to generate $4,800 in revenue for a full year, Arison sees the acquisition as a financial no-brainer as well. If the company achieves it’s baseline goal of 50,000 Grindr users getting PrEP through the app, it would generate $240 million in revenue annually.

Moving forward, Arison says the acquisition sets the brand up “for a much broader Grindr Health vision.” One example? Putting users in touch with health professionals who are part of or experts on LGTBQ+ health.

“I talk to so many people—myself included, honestly—who want a gay doctor and cannot get a gay doctor,” Arison says. “Over time, we can be in a place where we’re giving way more capability to our users to find gay doctors, and be able to connect with them virtually for their other healthcare needs.”

items.title: 🔓 [Fast Company] Paramount’s megamerger with Warner is set to close soon as judge approves settlement with 12 states
items.content_html:
A federal judge has granted Paramount’s settlement agreement with 12 states that sued over the company’s takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery, allowing the companies to soon close their $81 billion megamerger.

In a Wednesday order, U.S. District Judge Araceli Martínez-Olguín ruled that the proposed consent decree was a “fair, reasonable, and good faith approach to address the competitive harms” alleged by the states’ lawsuit. Paramount, which was bought by Skydance just last year, previously called the antitrust challenge the last hurdle ahead of closing its Warner merger.

The companies now expect to complete the deal on Oct. 6. Shortly after Martínez-Olguín’s ruling Wednesday afternoon, Paramount also announced Ynon Kreiz — who is toy giant Mattel’s current chief executive — will soon join as co-CEO alongside David Ellison.

In a statement, Ellison said Paramount’s merger with Warner marks a “transformational moment for our industry” and that he and his new co-CEO will lead a business that is “creator-first, tech-forward and built to scale globally.”

A Paramount-Warner marriage will bring together two of Hollywood’s last five legacy studios. HBO Max, a library full of titles including “Harry Potter” and cable networks such as CNN will also find themselves under the same roof with CBS, the likes of the “Top Gun” franchise and the Paramount+ streaming service.

That further concentrates power in an industry already run by just a handful of major players. And many critics of the deal have decried the states’ settlement, arguing the terms are too weak.

The final antitrust fight

Paramount touted clearances for its Warner acquisition from regulators worldwide over recent months, including the Trump administration’s Justice Department in the U.S.

But in July, top prosecutors from 12 states — led by California Attorney General Rob Bonta — sued to block the merger altogether. They alleged a Paramount-Warner combination would “extinguish competition” in Hollywood and lead to fewer choices for consumers, particularly movie theatergoers and cable customers.

Last week, the states agreed to settle those claims through new commitments from Paramount, including pledges to increase film production in the U.S. over the next five years, grant millions of dollars to a fund aimed at supporting workers displaced by the merger and establish new editorial monitoring of CNN and CBS.

Martínez-Olguín didn’t greenlight the terms right away — maintaining at a Thursday hearing that the court isn’t merely a “rubber stamp” on a settlement of this kind and that she, like many others, had questions. The judge granted outside critics of the settlement (including members of the Block The Merger coalition and the League of United Latin American Citizens) a brief window to share their opposition. She also instructed Paramount and the states to respond to concerns raised by Democratic Sen. Cory Booker.

By Wednesday’s order, however, she concluded that the hopes for settlement terms to go further “do not rise to the level of legal violations upon which the Court can reject the parties’ negotiated resolution.”

The Writers Guild of America, which had filed its own suit shortly after the states in July, also reached a settlement agreement with Paramount last week — concluding that it couldn’t continue its legal fight alone.

Ongoing criticism of the deal

The Block the Merger coalition on Wednesday maintained the states’ settlement was a “toothless” deal.

“In years to come, we’ll be able to point to this failure to put consumers over the monied interests of corporate consolidation as the tipping-point moment for media in this country,” Block the Merger said in a statement. But, the group added, “if there is one discernible benefit to the approval of this corporate takeover, it’s that people are now wide awake and paying attention — and their anger is not going to fade away.”

Before agreeing to settle, Bonta previously said the states would only consider “robust” structural remedies. The bulk of the eventual settlement outlined behavioral requirements, at least in the immediate future, with some potential “court enforceable” penalties if Paramount breaks promises down the road.

Even so, most of the company’s new commitments only last five years. Paula Blizzard, an attorney for California, said in Thursday’s hearing that the states eventually settled on terms that didn’t “last forever” because the industry is changing — while immediate divestments, or even the complete blocking of the deal that they initially demanded, could open the door to further acquisitions.

Among those new commitments include a pledge from Paramount to increase spending on film production in the U.S. — by at least an additional $1.5 billion over the next five years — and promises to release at least 30 films each year, a figure Ellison already touted earlier in his quest for Warner.

The states’ settlement would require Paramount to distribute 30 films in theaters each year for the next two years — and 32 films in each of the three years after that. The fine print notes that only 50% of those movies would have to be “produced or jointly produced” by the combined company. If Paramount fails to meet these film outputs, the states say it will have to divest from Miramax Studios and pay $30 million for each missed film toward healthcare and retirement trust funds associated with the Writers Guild of America and other industry unions.

Paramount also agreed to commit $47.5 million to help fund training and career development for workers displaced by the merger, again over the next five years ($9.5 million each year).

Meanwhile, when it comes to cable, the states’ settlement orders the company to negotiate deals for current Paramount-owned and Warner-owned basic cable channels separately over the next five years. If Paramount violates those terms, a court may order future divestments.

The company must also form a “News Editorial Independence Board” to monitor news operations at CBS and CNN within 180 days of completing its Warner acquisition. But critics point to editorial turmoil already seen at CBS under Skydance ownership — and aren’t convinced this new body will move the needle much.

Per court documents outlining the settlement’s terms, Paramount’s new editorial body will be made up of five “active or retired” journalists with at least 10 years of experience — all appointed by, and reporting to, the combined company’s board of directors for three-year terms. Beyond his CEO title, Ellison is Paramount’s current chairman and is set to remain in the top spot after the Warner acquisition closes.

While joining the rest of the states in the wider settlement, Colorado and Washington declined to sign off on the editorial board terms. And prosecutors like Connecticut Attorney General William Tong, who wanted a full divestiture of CNN and CBS, said last week he wished the deal could have gone further.

Including billions of dollars in debt, Paramount’s buyout of Warner is currently valued at about $111 billion based on outstanding shares.

—Wyatte Grantham-Philips, AP Business Writer

items.title: 🔓 [Fast Company] Mayor Mamdani just hired a bunch of ‘grocery store nerds’ to design NYC’s city-owned markets
items.content_html:
A consortium of designers, branding professionals, and grocery experts have been named to design a visual identity for New York City’s municipal grocery stores. Their goal? To make something that looks authentically New York.

New York City’s Economic Development Corp. (NYCEDC) said Tuesday it had selected four firms—Gander, Librarie, Noble Signs, and Seven Roots—to brand the city’s five forthcoming grocery stores, one for each borough.

Gander, the strategic branding firm behind visual identities for brands like the squeeze-bottle olive oil Graza and Yellow Bird hot sauce, will be the project lead and oversee research, strategy, naming, brand application, and brand development. Its inclusion suggests the finished product could borrow from the best practices of some of recent history’s most popular direct-to-consumer brands.

“We consider ourselves, for better or worse, grocery store nerds, and probably get way too much enjoyment out of wandering the aisles of grocery stores everywhere we travel,” Gander partner Mike McVicar tells Fast Company. Gander calls it a dream project since it’s a major civic project for the city the company loves, and it’s a grocery store.

“Our top priority is to help make this ambitious effort to address food insecurity in our city as wildly successful as possible, and ultimately help as many people as possible,” McVicar says. “That means building a brand that resonates with an infinitely diverse population of New York City that has really high standards.”

The boutique brand consultancy Librarie, which has advised brands like Stiller’s and the THC-infused beverage brand Cann, will co-lead on brand positioning, voice, copy, and naming. Librarie’s Fern Diaz says she hopes the consortium can turn the language around affordability and abundance from “words that can feel like policy jargon” into something that New Yorkers “feel and experience.”

The consultancy Noble Signs, a multidisciplinary creative studio that founded the New York Sign Museum, will consult on New York City history and culture so the final visual assets feel authentic to the city. Noble Signs has done work for Ace’s Pizza in Brooklyn and created hand-painted signage for New York City Councilman Justin Brannan’s Coney Island office.

Seven Roots, an independent grocery store design and development firm, will advise on food retail, operations, and integrating the brand into the physical retail environment. The only firm in the consortium that isn’t based in New York City, Seven Roots has developed independent grocery stores and community-owned food co-ops.

Seven Roots managing partner Heather Lazickas says the firm hopes their work contributes to a solid foundation for the NYC Groceries initiative, and she adds that the stores “will undoubtedly offer valuable lessons and inspiration for communities across the country working to strengthen their food access landscapes.”

The NYCEDC announced in May that it was opening requests for proposals for NYC Groceries. It was seeking brand research into industry trends and consumer habits, a visual identity and design application for the look of the stores, product private labeling, and branded merchandise, as well as architecture and engineering collaboration.

The four winning firms, which are subject to approval by the NYCEDC Board of Directors, will work together with NYCEDC and City Hall to develop the brand identity and execute on its other deliverables.

“Our municipal grocery stores should be a place every New Yorker recognizes and feels welcome in,” Deputy Mayor for Economic Justice Julie Su said in a statement. “With expertise and experience in branding, city history, and grocery retail, this team will help us deliver stores that make affordable food easy to find in every borough.”

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani campaigned last year on city-run grocery stores, and since taking office, he’s allocated $70 million in the city’s capital budget to the project. For a politician who’s shown a keen eye for smart, attractive visual branding in politics and government, that one of his signature campaign promises is getting a team of pros to make sure it’s branded well isn’t surprising.

But a welcoming visual identity will also be one key component to turning these municipal grocery stores into a success. NYCEDC CEO Anthony Shorris said selecting the right firms was an important step in “creating grocery stores that are welcoming, easy to recognize, and unmistakably New York.”

The first store, a 20,000-square-foot location at The Peninsula in the Bronx, is expected to open by 2027, and a second location has been identified for a 9,000-square-foot store in East Harlem. NYCEDC says all five stores are expected to be open by the end of Mamdani’s first term in 2030.
